items.title: Integral Jensen inequality for finite-dimensional convex losses
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $d\geq1$ and let $C$ be a
nonempty closed convex subset of $\mathbb R^d$, with closedness in the Euclidean
topology ([[def-metric-interior-closure-boundary]]) and convexity as in
[[def-convex-subset-of-euclidean-space]]. Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on
its Borel sets, and assume $\int_C\|a\|_2\,\mu(da)<\infty$, where $\|\cdot\|_2$
is the Euclidean norm from [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Define the barycenter
$b=\int_Ca\,\mu(da)$ coordinatewise and assume $b\in C$. If
$f:C\to[0,+\infty]$ is Borel measurable and convex, then
$$f(b)\leq\int_C f(a)\,\mu(da).$$
Here convexity uses [[def-convex-and-strictly-convex-functions-on-euclidean-sets]],
and the barycenter is the vector of coordinate integrals.
items.strategy: Direct proof via relative interior of the closed convex hull of the measure support, a supporting subgradient, and integration.

references.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §§5.1–5.3, PDF pp. 100–110
Peter Hoff, Statistical Decision Problems, §§4–5, PDF pp. 7–13

items.title: A prior and model kernel define a joint law
items.statement:
Let $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$ and $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$ be measurable spaces,
let $\pi$ be a probability measure on $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$, and let
$K:\Theta\times\mathcal A\to[0,1]$ be a probability kernel. For
$C\in\mathcal T\otimes\mathcal A$, write
$C_\theta=\{x\in\mathcal X:(\theta,x)\in C\}$ and set
$$J(C)=\int_\Theta K(\theta,C_\theta)\,\pi(d\theta).$$
Then $J$ is a probability measure on the product sigma-algebra, and for every
nonnegative product-measurable $h$,
$$\int_{\Theta\times\mathcal X}h(\theta,x)\,J(d\theta,dx)=\int_\Theta\left(\int_\mathcal Xh(\theta,x)\,K(\theta,dx)\right)\pi(d\theta).$$
In particular, $J(A\times B)=\int_AK(\theta,B)\,\pi(d\theta)$ for
$A\in\mathcal T$ and $B\in\mathcal A$.
items.strategy: Direct construction on product-measurable sets, countable additivity, then simple approximation and monotone convergence.

references.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §§5.1–5.3, PDF pp. 100–110
Peter Hoff, Statistical Decision Problems, §§4–5, PDF pp. 7–13

items.title: Loss functions and risk
items.statement:
Let $\mathsf E=((\mathcal X,\mathcal A),\Theta,(P_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta})$
be a statistical experiment ([[def-statistical-experiment]]), let
$(\mathsf D,\mathcal G)$ be a measurable action space, meaning a set with
a specified sigma-algebra ([[def-measurable-space]]), and let
$L:\Theta\times\mathsf D\to[0,+\infty]$ be a loss function whose section
$a\mapsto L(\theta,a)$ is $\mathcal G$-measurable for each $\theta$. A
randomized decision rule is a probability kernel $\delta$ from the data space
to the action space ([[def-randomized-procedure-as-a-markov-kernel]]). Its
**risk** at $\theta$ is the extended nonnegative number
$$R(\theta,\delta)=\int_{\mathcal X}\left(\int_{\mathsf D}L(\theta,a)\,\delta(x,da)\right)P_\theta(dx).$$
The inner integral is a measurable function of $x$, by
[[lem-procedure-action-law-is-measurable]], so the outer nonnegative integral
is defined by [[def-expectation-of-a-nonnegative-or-integrable-random-variable]].
A deterministic measurable rule is included by taking its point-mass action
kernel. No measurability on $\Theta$ is required for this definition.

references.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §§5.1–5.3, PDF pp. 100–110
Peter Hoff, Statistical Decision Problems, §§4–5, PDF pp. 7–13

items.title: Risk domination and admissibility
items.statement:
For two decision rules $\delta_0,\delta_1$ in one decision problem,
$\delta_1$ **dominates** $\delta_0$ if
$R(\theta,\delta_1)\leq R(\theta,\delta_0)$ for every parameter $\theta$,
with strict inequality for at least one $\theta$. A rule is **admissible** if
no decision rule dominates it; otherwise it is inadmissible. Risk is the
extended-valued function of [[def-loss-function-and-risk]]. Admissibility is
a pointwise comparison across the whole parameter set; it does not assert that
the rule minimizes risk at any particular parameter or under a global
criterion.

references.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §§5.1–5.3, PDF pp. 100–110
Peter Hoff, Statistical Decision Problems, §§4–5, PDF pp. 7–13

items.title: Bayes risk and minimax risk
items.statement:
Let $\Theta$ be a nonempty measurable parameter space, let the model be a
probability kernel from $\Theta$ to the data space, and let
$(\mathsf D,\mathcal G)$ be a nonempty measurable action space
([[def-measurable-space]]). Let $L:\Theta\times\mathsf D\to\overline{\mathbb R}$
be measurable from the product measurable space with sigma-algebra
$\mathcal T\otimes\mathcal G$ to the extended real line with its Borel
sigma-algebra, and assume $L(\theta,a)\geq0$ for all $(\theta,a)$
([[def-product-sigma-algebra-and-finite-product-sigma-algebras]],
[[def-measurable-function-between-measurable-spaces]], [[def-extended-reals]],
[[def-borel-sigma-algebra-on-the-extended-real-line]]). A **prior** $\pi$ is a
probability measure on $\Theta$. The risk function $\theta\mapsto R(\theta,\delta)$ is measurable
under these hypotheses by kernel integration
([[def-parameter-measurable-statistical-model-as-markov-kernel]],
[[thm-measurability-of-integration-against-a-kernel]]). The **Bayes risk** of
$\delta$ under $\pi$ is
$$r_\pi(\delta)=\int_\Theta R(\theta,\delta)\,\pi(d\theta)\in[0,+\infty].$$
Its **worst-case risk** is $R^*(\delta)=\sup_{\theta\in\Theta}
R(\theta,\delta)$, and the **minimax value** is
$$V_{\rm mm}=\inf\{R^*(\delta):\delta\text{ is a measurable randomized rule from data to actions}\}.$$
A rule is minimax if its worst-case risk equals this infimum. These definitions
make no assertion that a minimizer exists. Nonemptiness of $\mathsf D$ ensures
the rule class is nonempty: fixing any $a_0\in\mathsf D$ gives the constant
point-mass rule $x\mapsto\delta_{a_0}$.

references.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §§5.1–5.3, PDF pp. 100–110
Peter Hoff, Statistical Decision Problems, §§4–5, PDF pp. 7–13

items.title: Randomization does not improve convex action loss
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $d\geq1$ and let the
action space be a nonempty closed convex set $\mathsf D\subseteq\mathbb R^d$,
with its Borel sigma-algebra ([[def-measurable-space]]). Closedness is in the
Euclidean topology ([[def-metric-interior-closure-boundary]]) and convexity
uses [[def-convex-subset-of-euclidean-space]]. Let
$\delta(x,da)$ be a randomized decision rule and let $L(\theta,\cdot)$ be a
nonnegative Borel convex loss on $\mathsf D$
([[def-convex-and-strictly-convex-functions-on-euclidean-sets]]). Assume for
every $\theta$ that $\int_\mathsf D\|a\|_2\,\delta(x,da)<\infty$ and the
barycenter $b_\delta(x)=\int_\mathsf D a\,\delta(x,da)$ belongs to $\mathsf D$
for $P_\theta$-almost every $x$. Then there is a measurable deterministic
rule $d$ such that
$$R(\theta,d)\leq R(\theta,\delta)\qquad(\theta\in\Theta).$$
The barycenter is taken coordinatewise; finite first moment in the Euclidean
norm of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] makes each
coordinate integral finite. No claim is made for nonconvex action sets or when
the barycenter condition fails.
items.strategy: Direct: define the measurable barycenter rule and apply finite-dimensional integral Jensen pointwise before integrating each sampling law.

references.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §§5.1–5.3, PDF pp. 100–110
Peter Hoff, Statistical Decision Problems, §§4–5, PDF pp. 7–13

items.title: A posterior-risk minimizer minimizes prior risk
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a probability
kernel from a standard-Borel parameter space $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$ to a
standard-Borel data space $(\mathcal X,\mathcal A)$, where standard Borel means
measurably isomorphic to a Polish space
([[def-standard-borel-space]]). Let $\pi$ be a prior,
and let $L:\Theta\times\mathsf D\to[0,+\infty]$ be jointly measurable for a
measurable action space $(\mathsf D,\mathcal G)$. Let $J$ be the joint prior-data
law of [[lem-prior-and-model-kernel-define-joint-law]], let $M$ be its data
marginal, and let $\Pi_x(d\theta)$ be a regular posterior distribution of
$\theta$ given $x$ (the disintegration is supplied by
[[thm-disintegration-of-a-joint-law-on-standard-borel-spaces]]).
Define posterior risk
$$q(x,a)=\int_\Theta L(\theta,a)\,\Pi_x(d\theta).$$
Suppose a measurable deterministic rule $d^*:\mathcal X\to\mathsf D$
attains the posterior minimum for $M$-almost every $x$; that is,
$q(x,d^*(x))\leq q(x,a)$ for every $a\in\mathsf D$ on one $M$-full-measure
set. Then $d^*$ minimizes prior-integrated risk among all randomized decision
rules $\delta$:
$$r_\pi(d^*)\leq r_\pi(\delta).$$
No conclusion is asserted when a measurable posterior minimizer does not
exist. All risks may be $+\infty$.
items.strategy: Direct: disintegrate the prior-data law, use Tonelli to express posterior risk, then integrate the pointwise minimizing inequality against any action kernel.

references.title: Ryan Martin, Lecture Notes on Advanced Statistical Theory, §§5.1–5.3, PDF pp. 100–110
Peter Hoff, Statistical Decision Problems, §§4–5, PDF pp. 7–13

title: Loss, Risk and Decision Theory — Examples

items.title: Squared-error risk for a Bernoulli observation
items.statement:
Observe one Bernoulli variable $X\in\{0,1\}$ with parameter
$\theta\in[0,1]$, so $P_\theta(\{1\})=\theta$ and
$P_\theta(\{0\})=1-\theta$. Estimate $\theta$ by the rule
$d(X)=X$ under squared-error loss $L(\theta,a)=(a-\theta)^2$. Its risk is
$$R(\theta,d)=\theta(1-\theta),$$
which is zero at both endpoints and has maximum $1/4$ at $\theta=1/2$.
items.strategy: Direct finite verification of the probability law, measurable estimator, risk sum, and endpoint/maximal-risk cases.

items.title: Randomization lowers worst-case risk under zero-one loss
items.statement:
Let $\Theta=\{0,1\}$, let the data space contain one point with the same
sampling law at both parameters, and let the action space be $\{0,1\}$.
Under zero-one loss $L(\theta,a)=1_{\{a\ne\theta\}}$, the deterministic rule
that always chooses $0$ has risks $0$ and $1$, hence worst-case risk $1$.
The randomized rule that chooses each action with probability $1/2$ has risk
$1/2$ at both parameters and is minimax with value $1/2$.
items.strategy: Direct finite verification of the decision kernels and exact worst-case risks for every randomization probability.

items.title: A data-dependent rule dominates a constant rule
items.statement:
Let $\Theta=\{0,1\}$ and observe $X\in\{0,1\}$ with
$P_\theta(\{x\})=1$ when $x=\theta$ and zero otherwise. Under squared-error
loss, the constant rule $d_0(x)=0$ has risk $0$ at $\theta=0$ and $1$ at
$\theta=1$. The data rule $d_1(x)=x$ has risk zero at both parameters, so it
dominates $d_0$.
items.strategy: Direct finite calculation of both risk functions at both parameter values.

items.title: An open action set need not contain a posterior-risk minimizer
items.statement:
Every posterior expected-loss function on a nonempty open action space attains
its infimum.
items.strategy: Direct singleton posterior calculation and an explicit sequence approaching the unattained infimum.
